source: Owner message on 2026-10-31, answering question 6 of the UDA and Mission Control owner questions page, which asked whether to extend Mission Control's sending permission (its deployment lease) before it ran out on 2026-11-03.
owner_statement: 6 why don' we unlimit it, i don't see why sending permissions hould end
problem: Mission Control's deployment lease names the one relay host allowed to send, with an expiry. It was renewed by hand with a settings change and a restart, so sending would stop whenever a renewal was missed.
required_behavior: While Mission Control runs, its configured lease does not run out: the daemon renews it hourly when due, extending only the expiry once less than half of the renewal window remains.
An expired lease is never revived, and a configured successor lease stops renewal of the old one, so a takeover still waits out the old lease's expiry.
MISSION_CONTROL_SUBMISSION_LEASE_AUTO_RENEW=off switches renewal off; MISSION_CONTROL_SUBMISSION_LEASE_AUTO_RENEW_DAYS (2-60, default 14) sets the window.
basis: patterns/mission-control-multi-host-submission-scheduling.md, controlled takeover step 5, which binds a takeover to the old lease's expiry.
scope: Mission Control's submission-authority runtime and daemon, their tests and settings example, the multi-host scheduling pattern, this record, and its test.

origin.owner_outcome: Sending permission doesn't end while Mission Control runs.
origin.notes: The owner asked for no end at all. Renewal instead of no expiry is the assistant's choice: without an expiry, a controlled takeover could never complete, because step 5 waits for the old lease to run out.

execution_surfaces.note: Active after the next deployment of this code.

nonclaims: Renewal does not make the relay host healthy or prove it is the only sender; the single-active confirmation still comes from the lease and the takeover procedure.
If Mission Control is down for longer than the remaining lease, the lease runs out and needs a deliberate renewal or takeover.
